form.label: Case Work
form.description: Open a case on a detection, record what you found, and close it with a resolution. Nothing is overwritten: every note and decision stays as its own entry, so the reasoning survives the person who wrote it.

input.label: Your name (recorded on anything you write)

search.query: index=sigma_alerts | dedup sigma_rule_id, sigma_src_host, sigma_first_seen | eval case_id=substr(md5(sigma_rule_id."|".sigma_src_host."|".tostring(round(sigma_first_seen,0))),1,12) | stats count by case_id | join type=left case_id [ search index=sigma_cases | stats count as touched by case_id ] | where isnull(touched) | stats count

panel.title: Detections — select one to open or continue a case

search.query: index=sigma_alerts | dedup sigma_rule_id, sigma_src_host, sigma_first_seen | lookup sigma_rules sigma_rule_id OUTPUT sigma_technique_name | eval case_id = substr(md5(sigma_rule_id."|".sigma_src_host."|".tostring(round(sigma_first_seen,0))),1,12), when = strftime(sigma_first_seen,"%F %T"), technique = if(sigma_technique_name="","no technique mapped",sigma_technique_name) | join type=left case_id [ search index=sigma_cases | stats latest(case_status) as case_status, latest(case_resolution) as case_resolution by case_id ] | eval triage = case(isnull(case_status), "untriaged", case_status="resolved", "resolved: ".case_resolution, 1==1, "case open") | table when, sigma_src_host, sigma_rule, technique, sigma_level, triage, case_id, sigma_rule_id | rename when as "When", sigma_src_host as "Host", sigma_rule as "Rule", technique as "Technique", sigma_level as "Severity", triage as "Triage" | sort - "When"

format.colorPalette: {"untriaged":#fab219,"case open":#19C1EB,"resolved: false positive":#8A8A93,"resolved: true positive":#d03b3b,"resolved: benign expected":#0ca30c,"resolved: duplicate":#8A8A93}

input.label: What are you recording
input.choice: a note on what you found

input.label: Resolution
input.choice: false positive — the activity was legitimate
benign expected — known and accepted here

input.label: Say why, in your own words

html.div: Recorded as $analyst_tok$. Entries are appended, never replaced — correcting something means adding the correction, and both stay readable.

search.query: index=sigma_cases case_id="$c_id$" | eventstats latest(case_status) as latest_status | eval when=strftime(_time,"%F %T"), entry=case(case_action="open","opened the case", case_action="resolve","resolved as ".case_resolution, 1==1, case_action) | table when, case_analyst, entry, case_text | rename when as "When", case_analyst as "Who", entry as "What", case_text as "Said" | sort - "When"

| makeresults | eval case_id="$c_id$", case_action="$act_tok$", case_analyst="$analyst_tok$", case_text="$text_tok$", case_resolution=if("$act_tok$"=="resolve","$res_tok$",null()), case_status=if("$act_tok$"=="resolve","resolved", if("$prior_status$"=="resolved","resolved","open")), case_title="$c_rule$ on $c_host$", case_severity="$c_sev$", sigma_rule="$c_rule$", sigma_rule_id="$c_ruleid$", sigma_src_host="$c_host$", detection_time="$c_when$" | fields - _raw | collect index=sigma_cases sourcetype=sigma:case | eval result="written" | table result

html.div: If this panel reports that a risky command was not dispatched, Splunk is blocking collect from dashboards. That is the default and it is deliberate. docs/case-workflow.md has the single setting that changes it.

panel.title: Rules repeatedly resolved as false positive — allowlist these

search.query: index=sigma_cases case_action=resolve case_resolution="false positive" | stats count as times, dc(sigma_src_host) as hosts, values(sigma_src_host) as on_hosts, latest(case_text) as last_reason by sigma_rule, sigma_rule_id | where times >= 2 | sort - times | table sigma_rule, times, hosts, on_hosts, last_reason, sigma_rule_id | rename sigma_rule as "Rule", times as "Called a false positive", hosts as "Hosts", on_hosts as "On", last_reason as "Most recent reason", sigma_rule_id as "Add this id to sigma_allowlist.csv"

`sigma_case_state` | search $status_tok$ | eval opened=strftime(opened,"%F %T"), last_touched=strftime(last_touched,"%F %T"), outcome=coalesce(case_resolution,"not yet resolved") | table case_id, case_title, case_status, outcome, case_analyst, actions, opened, last_touched | rename case_id as "Case", case_title as "About", case_status as "Status", outcome as "Outcome", case_analyst as "Last touched by", actions as "Entries", opened as "Opened", last_touched as "Last entry" | sort - "Last entry"
